decision_reason: GIANT is a NASA Goddard optical-navigation software suite with current NASA catalog distribution, detailed installation and tutorial documentation, and mission-level use. Its public repo contains source, tests and documentation under Apache-2.0. NASA reports use through OSIRIS-REx proximity operations and ongoing GIANT development; the first public grant-bearing source commit is the 2021 initial public release.

government_provenance.note: NASA TechPort identifies GIANT as a GSFC IRAD project developed for OSIRIS-REx navigation verification and validation; NASA's Software Catalog separately identifies the exact GIANT product, GSC-19381-1.

public_source.note: The public NASA repository exposes GIANT Python source, tests, installation files and extensive documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository grant is Apache License 2.0. The 2021 initial-public-release commit adds this grant with substantive GIANT source and documentation: https://github.com/nasa/giant/commit/8576b12d8950c4d3bb73502eddba73b7600f819a.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact GSC-19381-1 entry describes the current version 2.0 product, says GIANT has been used throughout OSIRIS-REx proximity operations, and reports ongoing development. It also notes new user documentation and tutorials; the linked project documentation supplies installation guidance.

product_identity: Goddard Image Analysis and Navigation Tool (GIANT), a Python software suite for optical navigation, camera calibration, relative navigation, and mission image processing
geography: United States federal aerospace research and mission operations; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Maryland
license: Apache-2.0 for the nasa/giant source repository; third-party dependencies are separately licensed
status_note: Active: the public repository shows recent substantive source activity, and NASA's current exact-product catalog page says GIANT is continuously developed. NASA identifies its operational use in OSIRIS-REx and its role in OSIRIS-APEx mission planning.

decision_reason: The exact NASA GMSEC API is public and has substantial installation, configuration, language-binding and example documentation; NASA GSFC describes its current open-source distribution and mission ground-system role. However, the repository's NOSA.pdf does not identify an exact version in the material inspected, so eligibility under the required OSI-approved exact-license check and a defensible first licensed-source year remain unresolved.

government_provenance.note: NASA Goddard's GMSEC page identifies the center's GMSEC API and links the open-source distribution; the page attributes the development and maintenance to the GMSEC Development Team.

public_source.note: The assigned release URL resolves to this public NASA source repository, which contains API implementations, examples, build/install instructions and language bindings.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains a file named NOSA.pdf and source distribution metadata says NASA Open Source Agreement, but the exact grant version was not established from the repository copy. Do not assume NASA-1.3 from the filename or metadata; clearance requires the exact applicable OSI-approved agreement version or an authoritative repository-specific confirmation.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact GMSEC page identifies the open-source API distribution and provides official product context. The repo README gives concrete install/configuration guidance for supported operating systems, middleware brokers, language bindings and example programs.

product_identity: Goddard Mission Services Evolution Center (GMSEC) API, a multi-language application programming interface for NASA ground-system messaging middleware; not the separate government-only binary distribution or the whole GMSEC services suite
agency: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, GMSEC Development Team
geography: United States federal space-mission ground systems; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Maryland
license: Repository includes NOSA.pdf, but exact license version and applicability remain unresolved
status_note: Hold only for exact license identification and first eligible year. NASA's page distinguishes the public open-source API from a government-only binary distribution whose source is not provided.

decision_reason: NASA Ames' Generic Software Architecture for Prognostics (GSAP) is an identifiable framework with public source and documented scientific use, but the exact checked repository license PDF is titled NASA Public License Version 1, not the OSI-approved NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3. This custom grant fails the mandatory eligible-license check; a NASA catalog label of Open Source does not cure the repository license mismatch.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact software-catalog record ARC-17748-1A identifies the GSAP framework and its NASA provenance. The NASA-authored 2017 paper lists NASA Ames researchers and describes the framework.

public_source.note: The public nasa/GSAP repository exposes C++ framework source, examples, tests and documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository PDF identifies NASA Public License Version 1. The OSI-approved NASA grant is the distinct NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3); the custom NASA Public License v1 is not that approved license and no clear public-domain dedication was found.

primary_evidence.note: The peer-reviewed paper specifically introduces and evaluates GSAP as a software framework and includes a battery-prognostics case study; the NASA catalog identifies it as an open-source reusable framework and the repo has user documentation.

product_identity: Generic Software Architecture for Prognostics (GSAP), an extensible cross-platform framework and support library for building prognostics applications
geography: United States federal aerospace and prognostics research; NASA Ames Research Center, California
license: NASA Public License Version 1 in the exact repository PDF; not verified as an OSI-approved software license or a worldwide public-domain dedication
status_note: Reject under the exact-grant baseline. NASA's catalog page says its GitHub access is by request and signature, while the public repository contains a distinct NASA Public License v1; do not substitute the NASA-1.3 approval for this different grant. Reconsider only after an eligible repo-specific grant is supplied.

decision_reason: NASA Langley's Generic Transport Model DesignSim is a public Simulink flight-dynamics model listed in the NASA Software Catalog, but its exact LicenseAgreement.pdf is titled NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1, not the OSI-approved NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3. The repository does not include practical install/run guidance or a documented versioned code release; the NASA catalog says it requires the commercial Simulink environment and is not standalone. It therefore fails the exact eligible-license and product-maturity evidence gates.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact LAR-17625-1 catalog entry identifies this flight-dynamics simulation as a NASA open-source software release; the public repo describes the Generic Transport Model.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Simulink model source, README and LicenseAgreement.pdf without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository's agreement file identifies itself as NASA OPEN SOURCE AGREEMENT VERSION 1. OSI approval is specifically for NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3); version 1 is not the approved version and no separate eligible grant or worldwide public-domain dedication was located.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA catalog says the simulation must run inside MathWorks' commercial Simulink environment and is not standalone. The repository README only describes the model and cites a 2011 research paper; a versioned software release and practical user/install guidance or current exact-product use were not found.

product_identity: Flight Dynamics Simulation of a Generic Transport Model, a Simulink model of a 5.5%-scale generic transport aircraft for flight-control-law design and analysis
geography: United States federal aeronautics research; NASA Langley Research Center, Virginia
license: Repository LicenseAgreement.pdf states NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1; not verified as the OSI-approved NASA-1.3 grant
status_note: Reject as currently evidenced: exact repo grant is not the approved v1.3 text, and the source is a model requiring proprietary Simulink with no demonstrated versioned release/user procedure. NASA's catalog claims Open Source but does not override the grant attached to the checked files.

decision_reason: GUNNS is a NASA Johnson Space Center reusable C++ nodal solver and model library for fluid, thermal and electrical systems. NASA's current Version 19.X software-catalog and JSC modeling pages identify the exact product; repository v19.5 has NASA NOSA 1.3, source, examples, user and developer tutorials, setup, dependencies and release notes. The first public grant-bearing release source is 2021; its 2024 latest release is just over 24 months old, but the current NASA JSC and software-catalog listings establish continuing exact-product distribution and source parity, so the appropriate status is Maintained, not Active.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact MSC-26727-1 record identifies GUNNS Version 19.X as an open-source software product; the README and exact current NASA JSC modeling page identify NASA Johnson Space Center and its Simulation & Robotics Division.

public_source.note: The public repository contains C++ model source, tests, Draw.io assets, builds, examples, releases and user/developer documentation.

eligible_license.note: The exact source grant says NASA OPEN SOURCE AGREEMENT VERSION 1.3 and identifies designation MSC-26727-1, the GUNNS Version 19 source. NASA-1.3 is OSI-approved: https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3. The first public commit adds the grant with the v19.0 source: https://github.com/nasa/gunns/commit/039bc0f692b388bf9d23d92de2bedb9d9c919142.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current JSC Simulation & Modeling page lists GUNNS Version 19.X among related software. The exact NASA software-catalog release and public repository include a v19.5 release plus user setup, dependencies, tutorials and model-building guides.

product_identity: General-Use Nodal Network Solver (GUNNS), a reusable C++ library/toolset for modeling fluid, thermal and electrical flow circuits via nodal analysis
agency: NASA Johnson Space Center, Simulation & Robotics Division
geography: United States federal human-spaceflight modeling and simulation; NASA Johnson Space Center, Texas
license: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3 (NASA-1.3) for GUNNS Version 19; NASA identifies non-safety-critical status and external Trick/sim-bus dependencies are not included
status_note: Maintained: do not call Active based on the 2024-09-23 v19.5 release. NASA's current JSC modeling page and catalog still list the exact v19.x source product, and the repository's NASA designation/license matches that product. GUNNS does not include a complete simulation environment or the separate internal sim bus.
